name: HI-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Jill Tokuda running with large financial edge
Challenger Brenton Awa's minimal fundraising and cash
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~96%
model.rationale: Hawaii's second district leans heavily Democratic, and incumbent Jill Tokuda holds a dominant fundraising position with over $538,000 on hand against a challenger who has raised little and has under $8,000 remaining. Markets price this race at roughly 96% Democratic, consistent with the fundamentals-based expectation of a wide margin.
model.watch: Any late surge in challenger fundraising or outside spending, or a polling surprise, would be the main signal that this race is tightening.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Jill Tokuda, the Democratic incumbent, seeks a second term in a Hawaii district that leans about twelve points Democratic at the presidential level. She has raised more than $939,000 and holds over half a million dollars in cash, while Republican challenger Brenton Awa has raised roughly $129,000 with only about $7,700 remaining, leaving him little capacity to compete on air or on the ground.

No public general-election polling exists for this race, and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive. Prediction markets put Tokuda's chances near 96%. With the incumbent advantage, the district's partisan lean, and the financial imbalance all pointing the same direction, this race sits firmly in the safe Democratic column, though the absence of polling leaves some room for uncertainty about the exact margin.
